finding.claim: GET /rss passes the unvalidated `u` query parameter directly to URI.open, letting an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs and read the first 400 bytes of the response.
finding.sink: URI.open at app.rb:8 (open-uri server-side fetch), response returned via data[0, 400] at app.rb:9

trace.note: params[:u] passed straight to URI.open with no parsing, allow-list, or scheme check
open-uri performs the server-side request and .read returns the body
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No host allow-list, scheme check, or private/loopback IP-range check on this path. No redirect restriction (open-uri follows redirects, so an allowed URL can redirect internally). No DNS pinning (check-then-fetch pattern from case 12 would apply if a check were added). Not run; based on code reading. file:// and bare-path inputs also reach open-uri's local file path (related read issue).

verdict.guard_found: none. The TRUSTED host allow-list at app.rb:5 and the check at app.rb:13-14 apply only to the /trusted route, not /rss. The /rss handler at app.rb:7-9 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open with no validation.
verdict.reason: At app.rb:7-9, the unauthenticated `u` query parameter goes directly into URI.open(params[:u]) and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned, with no host, scheme, or IP check on that route; the only allow-list (app.rb:5, 14) is on /trusted.
